diagnosis:
All four rollouts reveal all three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3), cite them in justification_fact_ids, and settle with decisions that clearly reflect the information. The failures are entirely ENCODING MISMATCH problems — the checks expect exact strings or field values the model never produces verbatim, even though the underlying information is correctly used.

C1 (gated by PF1, failed 4/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check apparently expects the correction_response field to contain the exact phrase 'private correction' (matching PF1's wording 'private correction followed by exactly a five-minute library regulation break'). In every rollout the settlement encodes the concept as 'corrections will be delivered privately' (rollout 0), 'private, prearranged regulation breaks' (rollout 1), 'private redirection rather than public verbal corrections' (rollout 2), and 'private redirection to avoid triggering elopement' (rollout 3). The model consistently conveys private delivery of corrections but never uses the exact noun phrase 'private correction.'

C4 (gated by PF3, failed 4/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check apparently expects the family_update_method field to contain the exact phrase 'end-of-day' (matching PF3's wording 'end-of-day Spanish text messages'). In every rollout the model encodes the timing as 'text message' (rollout 0, with 'end-of-day' only in the commitment detail), 'text message at the end of each school day' (rollouts 1, 3), or 'text message sent at the end of each school day' (rollout 2). The settlement decisions field never contains the hyphenated exact string 'end-of-day.'

C6 (gated by PF1, failed 4/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check apparently expects the correction_response field to contain the exact phrase 'five-minute library regulation break' or a very close verbatim match. In every rollout the settlement's correction_response field says 'private redirection' or 'private, prearranged regulation breaks' without the words 'five-minute' or 'library.' The five-minute and library details are correctly captured in the separate regulation_break_minutes (5) and regulation_break_location (library) fields, but the correction_response field itself never includes the full phrase the check appears to require.

C7 (gated by PF2, failed 4/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check apparently expects the daily_reinforcement_minutes field or an associated text field to contain the exact phrase 'every school day' (matching PF2's wording 'ten minutes every school day'). In every rollout the settlement correctly sets daily_reinforcement_minutes to 10, but the 'every school day' frequency is encoded only in the commitment/plan_revision detail text (e.g., 'daily ten-minute reinforcement check'), not in the decisions field the check appears to inspect. The model uses 'daily' instead of 'every school day.'

C8 (gated by PF3, failed 4/4): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check apparently expects a formal communication commitment of a specific type or with specific wording that the model never produces. In every rollout the settlement includes a plan_revision commitment targeting the family communication change (e.g., 'Build in daily Spanish-language text messages to the caregiver at the end of each school day, replacing the discretionary family contact currently in the draft'), but the commitment type is 'plan_revision' or 'documentation' rather than whatever exact type string the check requires.

No rollout hit the turn cap. No TELEPATHY, NEVER REVEALED, REVEALED BUT UNUSED, or MISAPPLIED failures are present — the information is always disclosed, cited, and correctly applied. The problem is purely that five checks demand exact string matches the model does not produce naturally.
